articles.headline: SP push, RBI meetings mark Tata IPO saga
articles.summary: RTI responses reveal that Shapoorji Pallonji Group chairman Shapoor Mistry wrote to the Prime Minister's Office and RBI seeking intervention for an IPO of Tata Sons. Mistry argued for the listing on grounds of fairness. RBI records indicate at least 16 meetings between central bank officials and Tata executives occurred over four years regarding the group's core investment company status.

articles.headline: Govt eyes margin caps for cardiac drugs, antibiotics
articles.summary: The Centre is examining trade margin caps for essential medicines, including cardiac drugs, antibiotics, and treatments for diabetes and heart disease. The Department of Pharmaceuticals and NPPA are studying how such interventions could be structured. The move aims to reduce retail prices by 70-90% for patients, potentially reshaping India's $60-billion pharmaceutical industry.

articles.headline: India Street may face test from AI trade revival
articles.summary: Indian equities face a potential shift as global investors pivot back to artificial intelligence stocks following Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia. The Nasdaq 100's rally could challenge the recent revival in Indian markets, which had seen Sensex gain nearly 12% month-to-date. Foreign portfolio investors' interest in AI-heavy markets like South Korea and Taiwan may divert flows from India.

articles.headline: India plans new gas exchange to deepen futures trading
articles.summary: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is seeking proposals to establish a new natural gas exchange. The move aims to deepen futures trading and enhance energy security amid West Asia conflicts. The exchange will likely allow trading of petroleum products like jet fuel and naphtha, which are currently not traded on the Indian Energy Exchange or Multi Commodity Exchange.

articles.headline: Private projects announced jump 59% to ₹26.6 trillion in H1
articles.summary: New private sector project announcements surged 58.5% year-on-year to ₹26.6 trillion in the first half of FY27, according to CII. Manufacturing, electricity, and technology-related infrastructure are key drivers. The private sector's share of total announcements rose to 86.2% from 74.2% a year earlier, reflecting improved corporate balance sheets and government policy reforms.

articles.headline: States borrow ₹7 trillion from market in 8 months
articles.summary: Indian states have raised ₹7 trillion through market borrowings in the first eight months of FY27, approximately 12.5% more than the ₹6.2 trillion raised in the same period last year. Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, and Karnataka were the largest contributors. The RBI has indicated that states are expected to raise another ₹3.61 trillion in the October-December quarter.

articles.headline: India may review wheat export policy amid acreage concerns
articles.summary: The Indian government has initiated internal deliberations on reviewing the wheat export policy following a 15.3% drop in wheat acreage as of November 13. High domestic prices and low soil moisture levels have prompted officials to consider domestic food security before making any decisions. India banned wheat exports in May 2022 to control rising local prices.

articles.headline: Govt to review duties to boost economy
articles.summary: The government is conducting a comprehensive review of customs duties on various raw materials and intermediates to boost domestic manufacturing and exports. Targeted sectors include textiles, minerals, chemicals, and electronics. The review aims to mitigate the impact of rising global inflation and geopolitical frictions, while helping to rein in domestic price pressures.

articles.headline: Informal economy grew at record pace in Jul-Sep
articles.summary: India's unincorporated non-farm economy expanded at its fastest quarterly pace on record in July-September, driven by owner-operated businesses and self-employment. The number of establishments rose 18.8% year-on-year to 94.7 million, while employment grew 16.8% to 150.3 million. This surge follows the expansion of GST coverage and formalization efforts in the previous year.

articles.headline: PNGRB plans new framework to award gas pipeline projects
articles.summary: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board has proposed a new framework for awarding natural gas pipeline projects to ensure a 14% post-tax return on equity. The plan seeks to insulate investors from variations in throughput volumes, shifting the focus from transportation tariffs to construction costs. This aims to attract investment in India's expanding energy infrastructure.

articles.headline: Oil touches three-month lows before recovering
articles.summary: Global oil prices hit three-month lows on Tuesday due to signs of rising crude supply and reduced fears of immediate shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures gained 35 cents to $71.84 a barrel after falling earlier in the session. Analysts note that while geopolitical tensions remain, the market is currently well-supplied, tempering price volatility.

articles.headline: Sugar trade body urges govt to end stock limits
articles.summary: The All India Sugar Trade Association has requested the government to end sugar stock holding limits for traders and bulk consumers by November 30. The body cited improved supplies from the new crushing season as the reason for the request. The government had imposed the limits earlier this year to ensure adequate domestic availability and prevent price hoarding.

articles.headline: Can SpiceJet raise ₹5,500 crore to stay afloat?
articles.summary: Cash-strapped SpiceJet is attempting to raise ₹5,500 crore through equity and debt to settle liabilities and expand its fleet. The airline currently faces mounting operational lapses and a show-cause notice from the DGCA. Its market share has shrunk to 0.60% as many planes remain grounded. Success depends on investor confidence and the airline's ability to settle aircraft lessor claims.

articles.headline: Labour ministry launches unified portal for employment services
articles.summary: The labour ministry has launched a unified portal to bring employment exchanges, state sites, and private job portals onto a single platform. The platform aims to streamline the job-seeking process and match employers with suitable candidates more efficiently. However, experts suggest the success of the portal will depend on its ability to effectively regulate informal labour contractors.

articles.headline: Small firms grapple with big credit gap
articles.summary: Despite government schemes like Mudra and Stand-Up India, MSMEs in India face a financing gap of approximately ₹30 trillion. Sidhi estimates total credit demand at ₹64 trillion, but formal supply stands at only ₹34 trillion. While Mudra disbursements have grown, a shift toward larger-ticket loans and rising NPA levels among micro-enterprises remain significant risks to credit expansion.

articles.headline: Chalet Hotels charts 5-year growth plan
articles.summary: Chalet Hotels aims to triple its revenue by FY31 through a aggressive expansion strategy, including adding 1,200 rooms across the India and the Maldives. The company plans to fund the expansion from internal accruals and debts without raising fresh equity. Management believes the hospitality sector is entering a long-term growth cycle as domestic travel demand remains robust.

articles.headline: Wholsum eyes majority stake sale at ₹2,000 crore valuation
articles.summary: Wholsum Foods, the parent company of millet-based brand Slurrp Farm, is seeking a majority stake sale that would value the startup at ₹1,800-2,000 crore. The company has engaged JP Morgan as an advisor and is reportedly in talks with global FMCG majors like Nestle and ITC. The move comes as demand for healthy, nutrient-dense breakfast options surges in India.

articles.headline: Bharti's OneWeb seeks trial satcom spectrum renewal
articles.summary: Eutelsat OneWeb, backed by Bharti Enterprises, has applied to the Indian government for a renewal of its trial satellite spectrum. The company's previous trial license expired in October after it failed to demonstrate certain security compliance requirements. A new trial period is necessary for OneWeb to continue testing its broadband services before a commercial launch in India.

articles.headline: PE, VC bets at five-year high in October
articles.summary: Private equity and venture capital investments in India reached an eight-month high of $8.7 billion in October, driven largely by the $5.3-billion acquisition of IDBI Bank by Fairfax. According to EY, the volume of deals also rose 21% compared to the previous year. The data suggests that despite global economic headwinds, India remains a top destination for institutional capital.

articles.headline: Iffco-Tokio readies health product as it widens bets
articles.summary: Iffco-Tokio General Insurance plans to launch a new comprehensive health insurance product as it expands beyond motor insurance. The company aims to provide more extensive coverage and faster claim settlements to compete in the growing retail health segment. Health insurance currently contributes about 10% to its total premium, a figure it plans to significantly increase by FY28.

articles.headline: Quick commerce raises the bar for category managers
articles.summary: The rapid expansion of quick-commerce platforms like Zepto and Blinkit has led to a surge in demand for experienced category managers. These professionals, who oversee brand partnerships and inventory, are seeing salary hikes of 20-30% as platforms compete for talent. Vacancies for these roles have more than doubled since 2024, highlighting the industry's shift toward operational efficiency.

articles.headline: GSK India enters blood cancer space with Blenrep
articles.summary: GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals (GSK India) is expanding its oncology portfolio with the launch of Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin) for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Multiple myeloma is one of the most common haematological malignancies in India. Blenrep is the first-in-class B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) therapy to be approved for this condition in the country.

articles.headline: Why Sarvam is now renting out global AI chips
articles.summary: Sarvam AI, India's high-profile AI startup, has begun renting out its cloud-based computing power to other developers. The move follows the startup's acquisition of 4,096 Nvidia H100 chips through government-subsidized schemes. By renting out its surplus capacity, Sarvam aims to generate revenue while supporting smaller Indian startups that lack the capital to buy their own advanced hardware.

articles.headline: Conflict in West Asia brings wedding splurge back home
articles.summary: Ongoing conflicts in West Asia have prompted wealthy Indian families to shift their destination weddings from places like Dubai and Qatar back to luxury venues in India. Palace hotels in Rajasthan and five-star resorts in Goa are seeing a surge in bookings, leading to room tariff hikes of 15-30%. The shift is a boost for the domestic luxury hospitality and event management sectors.

articles.headline: IIFCL IPO to include OFS and fresh share issue
articles.summary: The government is preparing for the initial public offering (IPO) of India Infrastructure Finance Co. Ltd (IIFCL). The issue will include an offer-for-sale (OFS) by the government and a fresh issue of shares by the company. IIFCL, which provides long-term finance to infrastructure projects, has a loan portfolio of over ₹63,000 crore. The IPO is expected to hit the market in FY28.

articles.headline: Ikea pushes India profit timeline to FY29 amid losses
articles.summary: Swedish furniture major Ikea has revised its timeline to achieve profitability in India to FY29, a year later than previously targeted. The company continues to invest heavily in expanding its store network and e-commerce operations. For FY26, Ikea India reported a revenue increase of 14% to ₹2,100 crore but remains in the red due to high operational and expansion costs.

articles.headline: Higher fares leave Indian airlines with empty seats
articles.summary: Indian airlines reported a dip in passenger load factors (PLF) in October as higher airfares deterred travelers ahead of the festive season. The industry's average PLF dropped to 81.2% from over 86% in September. While airlines like IndiGo and Air India increased capacity, passenger growth failed to keep pace, suggesting that price-sensitive customers are cutting back on discretionary travel.

articles.headline: Aera rejects distance-based fees at Bhogapuram airport
articles.summary: The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (Aera) has rejected a proposal to levy distance-based user development fees (UDF) at the upcoming Bhogapuram airport in Andhra Pradesh. The regulator ruled that such a fee structure would be discriminatory and could disproportionately impact short-haul passengers. Instead, Aera has approved flat UDF rates that are more in line with other major airports.

articles.headline: Ventive plans ₹1,350 crore hotel expansion
articles.summary: Ventive Hospitality, a joint venture between Blackstone and Pune-based Panchshil Realty, plans to invest ₹1,350 crore to add 1,200 rooms to its luxury hotel portfolio. The expansion will be funded through internal accruals and will focus on high-demand markets like Goa and Mumbai. The company currently owns several marquee properties under brands like Ritz-Carlton and JW Marriott.

articles.headline: Diamond Power bets big on data centres
articles.summary: Diamond Power Infrastructure is pivoting its business to focus on supplying specialized cables for data centres. The company has secured orders worth ₹242 crore in the July-September quarter from major players like L&T and Sterling and Wilson. With India's data centre capacity expected to reach 3,860 MW by 2030, the company sees a multi-year growth opportunity in this high-margin segment.

articles.headline: Adani signs three-year copper supply deal with Attero
articles.summary: Adani Enterprises' copper unit has signed a three-year deal with Attero Recycling for the supply of copper scrap. Under the agreement, Attero will supply nearly 2,000 metric tonnes of copper scrap per month to Adani's Kutch Copper facility. The deal aims to reduce Adani's dependence on imported copper ore and supports its goals for a circular economy in the metals business.

articles.headline: OTTs craft interactive experiences around shows
articles.summary: Streaming platforms like Amazon MX Player and SonyLIV are introducing interactive features like live polling and rewards to engage viewers. Shows like 'Rise and Fall' allow viewers to vote on plot developments in real-time, blurring the line between watching and playing. These interactive elements aim to increase viewer retention and provide brands with more targeted advertising opportunities.

articles.headline: US blacklists Megaspeed after Nvidia spy scandal
articles.summary: The US Department of Commerce has added Singapore-based Megaspeed International to its trade blacklist. The move follows allegations that the company helped smuggle advanced Nvidia AI chips into China. The decision is part of a broader push by the Biden administration to tighten export controls on high-end technology that could be used to enhance China's military and intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Alice Huang had ties to China's intelligence network
articles.summary: Alice Huang, who was briefly the interim CEO of Nvidia, is under scrutiny for her alleged ties to Chinese intelligence. Investigations have revealed that Huang had close relationships with several Chinese officials and may have been involved in sharing sensitive technology information. The revelations have raised concerns about corporate espionage and the security of US technology firms.

articles.headline: Corporate America's rocky relationship with boardroom romance
articles.summary: A series of high-profile resignations at firms like Nvidia and McDonald's has reignited the debate over workplace romance and corporate ethics. Boards are increasingly taking a zero-tolerance approach to undisclosed relationships between executives and subordinates to prevent conflicts of interest. Experts suggest that clearer policies and more transparent reporting are needed to protect shareholders.

articles.headline: Opec+ faces year's most consequential supply decision
articles.summary: Opec and its allies are set to meet in Vienna to decide whether to roll over current production cuts or begin increasing supply in early 2027. Saudi Arabia and Russia are pushing for continued restraint to support prices, while several smaller members are eager to pump more. The decision will have a major impact on global oil markets and inflation trends for the coming year.

articles.headline: Amazon's rival to Starlink struggles to catch up
articles.summary: Amazon's Project Kuiper, a satellite-based internet service designed to rival SpaceX's Starlink, is facing significant launch delays. The company has only a handful of satellites in orbit compared to Starlink's 6,000. High launch costs and technical challenges have slowed progress, potentially leaving Amazon behind in the race to provide global broadband coverage from space.

articles.headline: Japan draws auto suppliers into major arms build-up
articles.summary: Japan is increasingly tapping its automotive industry to help build a domestic defense manufacturing base. Companies like Toyota and Denso are being encouraged to supply components for military drones and armored vehicles. The move is part of Japan's multi-year plan to double its defense spending and reduce its reliance on foreign weapons manufacturers amid rising regional tensions.

articles.headline: Chinese AI aspirants drawing big bets to take on DeepSeek
articles.summary: Chinese AI startups like Pragmatik Labs and Minimax are raising billions of dollars to challenge global leaders like DeepSeek. Investors are betting that these companies can leverage China's vast data sets and engineering talent to create world-class large language models. However, the sector faces challenges from US export bans on the high-end chips needed to train these models.

articles.headline: China halts critical mineral export ban
articles.summary: China has unexpectedly halted a planned ban on the export of certain critical minerals used in the production of semiconductors and electric vehicles. The move is seen as a gesture of goodwill as trade talks with the US and EU continue. However, Beijing has warned that it could reinstate the ban if other countries continue to impose restrictive trade policies on Chinese technology firms.

articles.headline: Realty outlook improves in Q2 on growth prospects
articles.summary: A survey of real estate developers and financial institutions by Naredco and Knight Frank shows that sentiment in India's realty sector improved in the second quarter of FY27. The index rose to 56 from 48, indicating that stakeholders are increasingly optimistic about the sector's growth over the next six months. Rising demand for both residential and commercial properties is driving the positive outlook.

articles.headline: Aluminium industry urges stable policy framework
articles.summary: The Aluminium Association of India has urged the government to establish a stable and long-term policy framework for the sector. The industry is seeking a clear roadmap for duty structures and investment incentives to help it reach its goal of becoming a $44-billion industry by 2030. Stable policies are seen as critical for attracting the large-scale investments needed to expand production capacity.

articles.headline: Auto majors announce price hikes amid rising input costs
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, and Hyundai have announced price hikes across their vehicle portfolios from January 2027. The companies cited a steady increase in the cost of raw materials and logistics as the primary reason for the move. Higher input costs have been squeezing the margins of auto manufacturers for several quarters, despite strong sales volumes.

articles.headline: IN-SPACe seeks more space orders for satellites and rockets
articles.summary: IN-SPACe, India's private space regulator, is actively seeking more orders for satellites and rockets from both domestic and international customers. The move aims to boost India's share of the global space market and support the growth of the local private space ecosystem. IN-SPACe is also working with the government to provide more funding and infrastructure for space startups.

articles.headline: Amazon launches 36 Leo satellites on Ariane 6 rocket
articles.summary: Amazon has successfully launched 36 low-Earth orbit (Leo) satellites for its Project Kuiper constellation using an Ariane 6 rocket. The launch is a major milestone for the company's plan to provide high-speed satellite internet to underserved communities around the world. Amazon aims to have half of its planned 3,236 satellites in orbit by mid-2029 to meet its license requirements.

articles.headline: A couple's Egypt trip on a budget of ₹3.23 lakh
articles.summary: A Bengaluru-based couple managed a 12-day trip to Egypt for just ₹3.23 lakh by planning well in advance and using travel hacks. Their itinerary included visits to the pyramids, Aswan, and Luxor. They saved money by using local transportation, staying in mid-range hotels, and booking their flights during off-peak periods. Their story highlights how international travel can be affordable for middle-class Indians.

articles.headline: JPMorgan and HSBC put digital gold to the test
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase and HSBC have completed a pilot program to test the use of digital gold tokens for institutional trading. The digital tokens are backed by physical gold stored in secure vaults and allow for faster and more transparent settlement of trades. The banks believe that digital gold could become a major new asset class for institutional investors looking to hedge against inflation.

articles.headline: Tokenized real estate: protecting the small investor
articles.summary: SEBI and RBI are working on new regulations to protect small investors in the growing tokenized real estate market. Tokenization allows investors to buy fractional shares of commercial properties, but the sector lacks transparency and clear legal frameworks. The proposed rules would require platforms to register with regulators and provide more detailed disclosures about property valuations and risks.

articles.headline: Assessing RBI's currency interventions in the rupee market
articles.summary: Critics argue that the RBI's frequent interventions to support the rupee have become too expensive and could hinder the currency's natural price discovery. However, the central bank maintains that its actions are necessary to prevent excessive volatility and ensure financial stability. Experts suggest that a more transparent intervention policy could help build market confidence and attract foreign capital.

articles.headline: Processes needed to keep data privacy feuds out of court
articles.summary: With the Digital Personal Data Protection Act now in effect, legal experts are urging companies to establish robust internal processes to handle data privacy complaints. Resolving disputes through internal mechanisms can save companies time and money and prevent costly litigation. A proactive approach to data privacy is also seen as critical for maintaining customer trust and avoiding heavy regulatory fines.

articles.headline: AI can significantly improve advice from law firms
articles.summary: Large language models are increasingly being used by law firms to automate routine tasks like document review and legal research. AI tools can analyze thousands of pages of legal documents in minutes, allowing lawyers to focus on more complex and high-value work. However, the use of AI also raises concerns about data security and the need for human oversight to ensure the accuracy of legal advice.

articles.headline: Wealth transfer is about more than simply ownership transfer
articles.summary: As India's wealthiest families prepare to transfer an estimated $1.5 trillion to the next generation, experts are emphasizing the importance of values-based succession planning. A successful wealth transfer involves not just passing on assets, but also ensuring that the next generation shares the family's vision and values. Formal family constitutions and trusts are increasingly being used to manage this transition.

articles.headline: Crushing China's AI dreams is a costly gamble for America
articles.summary: The US government's efforts to restrict China's access to high-end AI chips could have a significant impact on global technology supply chains. While the restrictions are designed to protect US national security, they could also lead to higher costs for US firms and accelerate China's efforts to develop its own domestic chip industry. Experts warn that the move could lead to a decoupling of the global AI sector.

articles.headline: Labour survey: some segments might be getting missed
articles.summary: A review of India's Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) suggests that it may be under-reporting the number of workers in the informal and gig sectors. The current methodology may not fully capture the work of seasonal migrants and home-based workers, leading to an incomplete picture of the labour market. Improving the accuracy of the survey is critical for developing effective employment policies.

articles.headline: RBI Reduces Dollar Sales as Foreign Inflows Strengthen Rupee
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India lowered dollar sales to $2.56 billion in early November, down from $22.14 billion in October. This shift follows record foreign portfolio inflows of over $14 billion into Indian equities, which helped the rupee gain 2% during the month. Analysts expect the RBI to become a net buyer of dollars if the rupee continues to strengthen toward the 90-91 per dollar range.

articles.headline: Air India Overhauls Senior Management to Drive Financial Turnaround
articles.summary: Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam is restructuring the carrier's leadership team to include experienced airline professionals. Nipun Aggarwal, the current commercial chief, may transition to other roles within the Tata Group. The airline reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 22,238 crore for FY26, more than double the previous year, as global headwinds and operational costs hit performance.

articles.headline: Venture Capitalists Increase Investments in India’s Defence Technology Sector
articles.summary: Mainstream investors like Elev8, Peak XV, and Nexus are betting on Indian defense startups amid a government push for indigenization. Constelli is in talks for a Rs 300-400 crore round, while firms like Parsec Aerospace and Hical Technologies seek funding for drone and engine systems. The government has reserved Rs 1.39 lakh crore for domestic defense procurement in FY27.

articles.headline: IT Unions Demand National Policy to Protect Workers from AI Layoffs
articles.summary: Workforce experts and unions are calling for a government framework to mandate severance and reskilling standards for employees displaced by AI automation. The proposed rules would require firms to track AI-related job eliminations and prioritize internal redeployment. Currently, the industry lacks uniform standards for severance or advance notice for roles compressed by AI.

articles.headline: Tata Electronics Negotiates EPC Partnerships for Assam Chip Plant Phase 2
articles.summary: Tata Electronics is in talks with global engineering and construction firms for the second phase of its Rs 27,000 crore semiconductor assembly and test facility in Jagiroad, Assam. The greenfield project, developed with partner TCE, has begun trial runs. Phase 2 plans include expanding the 171-acre campus to increase indigenous manufacturing capacity.

articles.headline: Narendra Rathi Leaves SoftBank to Launch Public Markets AI Fund
articles.summary: Narendra Rathi, a director at SoftBank's India team, is exiting to start a fund focused on India’s AI infrastructure. The fund will target public companies, including data center providers and industrial firms, gaining from the AI build-out. Rathi is in discussions with family offices and founders for backing, joining a trend of senior VC investors starting independent firms.

articles.headline: Pixxel to Set Up Mega Satellite Manufacturing Hub in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Space tech startup Pixxel is establishing 'GigaPixxel,' a 250,000-sq-ft satellite manufacturing facility near Bengaluru’s international airport. The hub, expected to be operational by 2027, will produce up to 200 satellites annually by mid-2028. It will primarily cater to external customers, including government and commercial agencies, expanding Pixxel's current local capacity.

articles.headline: Australia Toughens Digital Duty of Care Law with Global Revenue Fines
articles.summary: The Australian government has increased proposed penalties for Big Tech companies to up to 5% of global revenue under its new Digital Duty of Care law. The legislation compels social media sites and AI providers to build safety into products to reduce online harm. The bill is expected to pass Parliament this week, marking a significant regulatory shift for global technology firms.

articles.headline: New-age Consumer Companies Use Efficiency to Protect Q2 Margins
articles.summary: Despite rising raw material and crude-linked costs, listed new-age firms like Nykaa and Lenskart have maintained profitability through scale and backward integration. Nykaa’s gross margin rose to 46%, while Lenskart improved domestic margins to 64%. Conversely, Honasa Consumer and Wakefit saw slight margin declines due to intense competition and polyol price inflation.

articles.headline: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari Vows to Ease Industrial Roadblocks
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari stated that the state is moving past 'fear psychosis' and toward industrial transformation. Speaking at an ET event, he revealed daily discussions with business leaders to resolve land acquisition issues and eliminate block-level corruption. Large investments from the Ambani, Adani, and Jindal groups are reportedly in the pipeline for the state.

articles.headline: Banks Alert RBI to Cyber Risks from NBFC Pre-authorisation Payments
articles.summary: High-street banks have flagged risks associated with 'pre-authorisation' mechanisms used by NBFCs and fintechs to move money from bank accounts. The host-to-host system lacks two-factor authentication, making it vulnerable to hackers who can initiate fraudulent payouts. Banks have asked the RBI and I4C to curb these arrangements to prevent systemic cyberattacks.

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party Rejects Congress Demand for 100+ Seats in UP
articles.summary: The Samajwadi Party has hardened its stance in seat-sharing talks, offering Congress only 26 seats for the Uttar Pradesh elections and publicizing the offer. SP leaders cited the 2022 performance as the basis for the allocation, while Congress leaders expressed dissatisfaction. Tensions escalated as SP unilaterally announced candidates for five seats, including two claimed by Congress.

articles.headline: India and Nepal to Develop Border SEZs and Hydropower Infrastructure
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepalese counterpart Balen Shah agreed to build special economic zones and industrial parks near their borders to link manufacturing supply chains. India will also encourage investment in Nepal's hydropower and transmission systems. The two nations aim to finalize arrangements to boost investor confidence and integrate UPI-based retail payments.

articles.headline: GSK Bets on Strategic Indian Role for Global Clinical Trials
articles.summary: GSK Pharma has elevated India to a strategic hub for global oncology clinical trials, aiming for a revenue of up to Rs 1,200 crore from the segment in three years. The firm recently launched the blood cancer drug Blenrep in India within 12 months of US FDA approval. GSK is leveraging its global capability centers in Bengaluru and Hyderabad to expedite drug development and launches.

articles.headline: Blackstone Ropes in Ritesh Kumar as Partner for India Insurance Venture
articles.summary: Blackstone has roped in former HDFC Ergo MD Ritesh Kumar as a 10% shareholder in its proposed Indian general insurance venture. He joins Anuj Tyagi, who also holds a 10% stake, while Blackstone retains 80%. The venture, which has filed for a license with Irdai, plans to use an AI-native operating model and an initial capital commitment of up to Rs 200 crore.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to Hear Activists Imam and Khalid’s Bail Pleas
articles.summary: The Supreme Court is set to hear bail applications from activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid challenging a Delhi High Court order in a UAPA case. The petitions involve legal arguments regarding the denial of bail in cases linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The outcome is expected to impact judicial interpretations of anti-terror law detention standards.

articles.headline: Seven Fishermen from Andhra Pradesh Missing off Odisha Coast
articles.summary: Search operations are underway for seven fishermen from Uppada village who went missing after their boat lost contact near Paradip Port on November 19. The Coast Guard is using ships and helicopters to trace the vessel, which set out on November 4. Andhra Pradesh CM Naidu confirmed that GPS and transponder signals have been lost, and families have been briefed on the situation.

articles.headline: Thiruparankundram Temple Defies Supreme Court Order on Deepam Lighting
articles.summary: Authorities at the Thiruparankundram hill temple lit the 'maha deepam' at the traditional mandapam instead of the 'deepathoon' pillar, defying an interim Supreme Court order. The court had allowed lighting the lamp on the controversial pillar as a one-time arrangement. Protests erupted outside the temple, and the BJP criticized the move as an insult to Hindu sentiments.

articles.headline: NIIF Infrastructure Finance Raises Rs 800 Crore via NCDs
articles.summary: NIIF Infrastructure Finance has raised Rs 800 crore through the issuance of five-year non-convertible debentures. The NCDs carry an interest rate of 8.48% per annum. The funds are expected to support the company’s infrastructure financing projects. This marks a successful capital raise in the domestic debt market for the sovereign-linked investment manager.

articles.headline: Anthropic Shares Fall Below IPO Price Amid Broader Tech Selloff
articles.summary: Anthropic PBC saw its shares slide below their $83 initial public offering price on Tuesday, trading at $83.39 in premarket sessions. The decline follows a volatile Nasdaq debut where the stock initially surged to $111.50. The reversal adds to concerns about high AI valuations as the S&P 500 enters correction territory and major tech server makers guide for weaker margins.

articles.headline: Lord’s Mark Industries Licensed for Radiation-Free Breast Cancer Screening
articles.summary: Lord’s Mark Industries has secured a manufacturing license for its proprietary radiation-free breast cancer screening device. The wearable system uses thermal sensors to identify biophysical abnormalities. With a target price of under Rs 700 per test, the company aims to make early screening accessible across India through partnerships with hospitals and government schemes by January 2027.

articles.headline: Passive Mutual Funds Dominate New Launches but Active Funds Draw Money
articles.summary: In the first seven months of FY27, passive schemes accounted for 63% of mutual fund new fund offers (NFOs) but garnered less than 19% of total money raised. Active funds raised Rs 14,200 crore compared to Rs 3,200 crore for passive ones. The trend reflects Indian investors' preference for actively managed funds that have historically outperformed benchmarks despite higher costs.

articles.headline: ITAT Rules Tata Sons Can Claim Deductions on Group Investment Interest
articles.summary: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal upheld Tata Sons’ claim that interest paid on borrowings for group company investments is a business expenditure. The tribunal rejected the tax department's attempt to disallow Rs 1,498 crore in interest for FY14. It ruled that Tata Sons’ role as an investment-holding company constitutes an active business beyond merely earning passive dividends.

articles.headline: Egg Prices Drop 20% Following Bird Flu Outbreak in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: Ex-farm egg prices have declined by 10-20% as bird flu in Tamil Nadu halted exports, causing a domestic supply glut. Seasonal demand in South India has also softened during the month of Karthik. Farmers face squeezed margins as production costs remain high, with maize and soybean feed prices rising up to 50% from the previous year.

articles.headline: Luxury Automakers Expand Electric Portfolios as Indian Demand Grows
articles.summary: Luxury carmakers like BMW and Mercedes-Benz are increasing EV options in India, with electric models now contributing up to 25% of some sales ranges. Mercedes-Benz’s electric GLC is sold out until 2027, while BMW’s i7 makes up half of its 7 Series sales. New entrants like Hyundai’s Genesis and JSW MG Motor’s Cyberster are further heating up the premium EV segment.

articles.headline: Agentic Commerce: AI Prepares to Handle Independent Digital Transactions
articles.summary: India's digital payments industry is exploring 'agentic commerce,' where AI agents independently complete purchases for users. Protocols like NPCI’s Unified Agentic Protocol and Pine Labs’ P3P aim to standardize how buyer and seller agents interact securely. While the technical foundation exists through UPI, challenges remain regarding liability, bot detection, and user trust.

articles.headline: Coca-Cola Returns to Human-Centric Ads for 2026 Holiday Season
articles.summary: Coca-Cola has released its 2026 holiday advertisement 'Enjoy Joy,' opting for human actors and traditional filming over the AI-generated imagery used in recent years. The move follows criticism of its 2024 and 2025 AI-led spots. The new campaign revives the 1971 'Hillside' jingle and focuses on family connections, reflecting a broader marketing shift back toward authentic human creativity.

articles.headline: CKB Global Logistics Opens New Built-to-Suit Warehouse in Gujarat
articles.summary: CKB Global Logistics has established a 113,000-sq-ft rack-supported warehouse in Kheda, Gujarat. The facility offers 27,000 pallet positions and features solar power and FSSAI approval. Designed for a long-standing client, the facility marks CKB’s transition into specialized 3PL warehousing. It integrates narrow-aisle operations and advanced fire protection to support modern supply chain needs.

articles.headline: WowTruck Targets Rs 220 Crore Revenue by FY27 with National Expansion
articles.summary: Trentar Group's logistics arm, WowTruck, is transforming into a national integrated logistics platform with a revenue goal of Rs 220 crore. The firm manages over 45,000 trucks and 350,000 sq ft of warehousing. It aims for a positive PAT margin by focusing on tech-led operations, including AI route optimization and digital twin technology for sectors like automotive and life sciences.

articles.headline: Government Announces New Economic Stimulus Package
articles.summary: The government has unveiled a comprehensive economic stimulus package aimed at boosting various sectors and creating employment opportunities. The package includes tax breaks for small businesses and investment incentives for key industries. Economists are currently analyzing its potential impact on the national GDP and inflation rates.

articles.headline: National Sports Federation Initiates Talent Identification Program
articles.summary: The National Sports Federation has launched a new nationwide program to identify and nurture young athletic talent. The initiative will focus on grassroots development in rural and urban areas, providing specialized training and infrastructure. The goal is to prepare athletes for future international competitions.

articles.headline: Key Reforms Proposed for Higher Education System
articles.summary: A high-level committee has submitted recommendations for significant reforms in the higher education system. Proposals include curriculum updates, teacher training enhancements, and increasing access to digital learning resources nationwide. Public feedback is being gathered for the proposals.

articles.headline: Public Health Advisory Issued for Monsoon Season Diseases
articles.summary: A public health advisory has been issued in anticipation of the monsoon season, highlighting preventative measures against waterborne and vector-borne diseases. Local health centers are being equipped to handle potential outbreaks, and awareness campaigns are underway to educate the public on hygiene and sanitation practices.

articles.headline: New Policy Framework for Sustainable Urban Development
articles.summary: The Ministry of Urban Development has introduced a new policy framework focusing on sustainable urban development. It emphasizes green infrastructure, efficient public transport, and waste management systems for growing cities. The policy seeks to create more livable and environmentally friendly urban spaces for future generations.

articles.headline: Opposition Parties Criticize Government's Recent Decisions
articles.summary: Opposition parties have strongly criticized the government's recent decisions regarding several national issues. They accuse the ruling party of failing to address core public concerns and demand greater accountability. Political analysts predict heated debates in the upcoming parliamentary session, potentially impacting policy implementation.

articles.headline: Cultural Festival Showcases Traditional Indian Arts
articles.summary: A vibrant cultural festival is underway, featuring a diverse array of traditional Indian performing arts, crafts, and culinary delights. Artists from across the country are participating, attracting a large audience. The festival aims to promote and preserve India's rich cultural heritage while fostering inter-community dialogue.

articles.headline: Judiciary Addresses Backlog with New Case Management System
articles.summary: The judiciary is implementing a new digital case management system to tackle the significant backlog of cases. The system is expected to streamline court processes, improve efficiency, and ensure faster dispensation of justice. Training for legal professionals is ongoing, anticipating a smoother transition to the new platform.

articles.headline: Local Elections See High Voter Turnout in Key Constituencies
articles.summary: Local elections witnessed an exceptionally high voter turnout in several key constituencies, signaling strong public engagement in democratic processes. Early results indicate close contests in many wards, with various political parties vying for control of municipal bodies. Final results are awaited by evening.

articles.headline: Environment Ministry Launches Campaign for River Clean-up
articles.summary: The Environment Ministry has initiated a major nationwide campaign focused on cleaning up polluted rivers and water bodies. The campaign will involve community participation, awareness programs, and strict enforcement of anti-pollution regulations. The long-term goal is to restore ecological balance and water quality.

articles.headline: Technological Advancements in Agriculture Boost Crop Yields
articles.summary: New technological advancements are transforming the agricultural sector, leading to significant increases in crop yields and improved farming efficiency. Innovations include precision farming techniques, drone-based surveillance, and weather forecasting tools. Farmers are embracing these changes to enhance productivity and income.

articles.headline: Retail Sector Shows Resilience Amidst Economic Fluctuations
articles.summary: Despite recent economic fluctuations, the retail sector has demonstrated remarkable resilience, driven by strong consumer demand and innovative business strategies. Online sales continue to surge, complementing traditional brick-and-mortar stores. Analysts project a steady growth trajectory for the sector in the coming quarter.

articles.headline: International Summit on Climate Change Concludes with New Pledges
articles.summary: An international summit on climate change concluded with several nations making new pledges to reduce carbon emissions and invest in renewable energy. Delegates emphasized the urgency of global cooperation to combat climate crisis and protect biodiversity. Discussions also focused on technology transfer to developing nations.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Delivers Landmark Verdict on Property Rights
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has delivered a landmark verdict clarifying complex issues related to ancestral property rights. The ruling is expected to have far-reaching implications for countless families and sets a new precedent in property law. Legal experts are closely examining the details of the judgment for wider application.

articles.headline: Scientific Breakthrough in Disease Treatment Research
articles.summary: Scientists have announced a significant breakthrough in disease treatment research, opening new avenues for therapies against previously incurable conditions. Early clinical trials show promising results, leading to optimism for future medical interventions. Further research and regulatory approvals are still required.

articles.headline: Government Launches Digital Literacy Program for Rural Areas
articles.summary: The government has initiated a new digital literacy program aimed at empowering rural populations with essential computer and internet skills. The program will establish community learning centers and provide training to bridge the digital divide. It seeks to enhance economic opportunities and social inclusion.

articles.headline: Agricultural Export Sector Experiences Significant Growth
articles.summary: India's agricultural export sector has recorded significant growth over the past year, driven by increased international demand and improved domestic production. New trade agreements and quality control measures have further boosted the sector's performance. The government plans to support further expansion.

articles.headline: National Road Safety Campaign Launched to Reduce Accidents
articles.summary: A nationwide road safety campaign has been launched with the goal of reducing traffic accidents and promoting safer driving habits. The campaign involves public awareness initiatives, stricter enforcement of traffic laws, and improvements in road infrastructure to enhance safety for all commuters.

articles.headline: Banking Sector Sees Consolidation and Digital Transformation
articles.summary: The banking sector is undergoing a period of consolidation, with several mergers and acquisitions announced, alongside a rapid digital transformation. Banks are investing heavily in FinTech solutions and online services to meet evolving customer demands and improve operational efficiency. This will reshape the financial landscape.

articles.headline: Wildlife Conservation Efforts Show Positive Results
articles.summary: Recent wildlife conservation efforts across national parks and sanctuaries are showing positive results, with an increase in the population of several endangered species. The success is attributed to stricter anti-poaching measures, habitat restoration, and community involvement in protection initiatives.

articles.headline: International Relations Strengthened Through Diplomatic Engagements
articles.summary: India's international relations have been further strengthened through a series of recent diplomatic engagements and bilateral talks. Agreements were signed on trade, security, and cultural exchange, fostering deeper ties with partner nations. These initiatives aim to promote regional stability and economic cooperation.

articles.headline: Startup Ecosystem Thrives with Government Support
articles.summary: The startup ecosystem in India continues to thrive, fueled by robust government support, venture capital investments, and a growing pool of skilled talent. Innovations are emerging across diverse sectors, including AI, renewable energy, and e-commerce. This fosters job creation and economic diversification.

articles.headline: Healthcare Sector Sees Major Investment and Expansion
articles.summary: The national healthcare sector is experiencing significant investment and expansion, with new hospitals and medical facilities being developed. Focus is on improving access to quality healthcare, especially in underserved areas, and integrating advanced medical technologies for better patient outcomes. Public-private partnerships are key.

articles.headline: Political Leaders Address Public Gatherings Ahead of Elections
articles.summary: Political leaders are actively addressing large public gatherings across the nation, outlining their visions and electoral promises ahead of upcoming elections. Campaigns are intensifying, with a focus on key issues such as employment, economic stability, and social welfare programs. Voter engagement is high.

articles.headline: New Guidelines for Corporate Social Responsibility Announced
articles.summary: New guidelines for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives have been announced, encouraging businesses to increase their contributions to social and environmental causes. The framework aims to ensure greater accountability and impact of CSR activities, promoting sustainable business practices across industries.

articles.headline: Comprehensive Report on National Development Goals Released
articles.summary: A comprehensive report detailing progress on national development goals has been released, highlighting achievements and areas requiring further attention. The report covers various indicators including poverty reduction, literacy rates, and environmental sustainability. It provides a roadmap for future policy interventions and resource allocation.

articles.headline: Debate on Data Privacy and Digital Rights Intensifies
articles.summary: The debate surrounding data privacy and digital rights has intensified, with lawmakers and privacy advocates calling for stronger regulations. Discussions involve balancing national security concerns with individual liberties in the digital age. A new legislative framework is being considered to address these complex issues.

articles.headline: Renewable Energy Sector Attracts Major Foreign Investment
articles.summary: The renewable energy sector has become a magnet for major foreign investment, driven by favorable government policies and growing demand for clean energy. Projects in solar and wind power are expanding rapidly, contributing to energy security and environmental sustainability. This will boost green jobs.

articles.headline: Tourism Sector Rebounds with Increased Tourist Arrivals
articles.summary: The tourism sector is experiencing a robust rebound, with a significant increase in both domestic and international tourist arrivals. New promotional campaigns and improved infrastructure are contributing to its recovery. The revival of tourism is expected to boost local economies and hospitality industries nationwide.

articles.headline: New Medical Research Focuses on Rare Diseases
articles.summary: Medical researchers are intensifying their focus on rare diseases, aiming to develop new diagnostic tools and treatment protocols. Funding has been allocated for specialized research centers and collaborative projects with international institutions. The goal is to provide hope for patients with limited options.

articles.headline: Global Market Volatility Impacts Local Stock Exchanges
articles.summary: Global market volatility has had a noticeable impact on local stock exchanges, leading to fluctuations in investor confidence. Analysts are closely monitoring international trends and advising caution amidst the uncertainty. The central bank is considering measures to stabilize the domestic financial markets proactively.

articles.headline: Education Technology Integration in Classrooms Expands
articles.summary: The integration of education technology in classrooms is rapidly expanding, with more schools adopting digital learning tools and online platforms. This aims to enhance interactive learning experiences and cater to diverse student needs. Teacher training is a crucial component for successful implementation across all levels.

articles.headline: Local Government Enhances Public Transportation Networks
articles.summary: Local governments are significantly enhancing public transportation networks to improve connectivity and reduce traffic congestion. New routes, upgraded facilities, and increased fleet sizes are part of the plan. These initiatives aim to provide convenient and affordable commuting options for urban residents, boosting efficiency.

articles.headline: Film Industry Grapples with Changing Audience Preferences
articles.summary: The film industry is currently navigating a period of significant change, grappling with evolving audience preferences and the rise of digital streaming platforms. Producers are experimenting with new content formats and distribution strategies to capture market share. This shift is reshaping traditional filmmaking.

articles.headline: International Aid Programs Target Poverty Alleviation
articles.summary: Several international aid programs have been launched, specifically targeting poverty alleviation and sustainable development in vulnerable regions. These initiatives focus on improving access to education, healthcare, and clean water. The coordinated efforts aim to empower local communities for long-term self-sufficiency.

articles.headline: Cybersecurity Threats Increase, Prompting New Protective Measures
articles.summary: Cybersecurity threats are on the rise, prompting governments and corporations to implement new protective measures. Investments in advanced security technologies and expert training are increasing to safeguard critical infrastructure and personal data. Public awareness campaigns also stress online safety practices.

articles.headline: Archaeological Discoveries Shed Light on Ancient Civilizations
articles.summary: Recent archaeological discoveries are providing unprecedented insights into ancient civilizations and historical trade routes. Excavations have unearthed artifacts and structures that reveal complex societal structures and advanced technologies of the past. These findings enrich our understanding of human history and cultural evolution.

articles.headline: Government Prioritizes Skill Development for Youth Employment
articles.summary: The government is prioritizing skill development initiatives to enhance youth employability and meet industry demands. New vocational training centers and apprenticeship programs are being established across various sectors. The aim is to equip young individuals with relevant skills for the modern job market.

articles.headline: ICC rejects Shubman Gill's saliva-shining plea
articles.summary: The International Cricket Council (ICC) will not reverse its ban on applying saliva to shine the ball, despite calls from Indian captain Shubman Gill to allow the practice again.

articles.headline: Jennifer Garner praises Ben Affleck's co-parenting
articles.summary: Jennifer Garner expressed admiration for Ben Affleck's co-parenting approach ten years after their divorce, calling him a 'great dad'.

articles.headline: Two arrested over burglary at Prince William's country home
articles.summary: UK police arrested two men on suspicion of burglary and trespassing at Sandringham estate's Anmer Hall, the country home of Prince William and Princess Catherine.

articles.headline: Scientists discover oldest quasar yet, formed 630m years after Big Bang
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered the most distant quasar yet, dating back to 630 million years after the Big Bang, a record-breaking early cosmic development. The quasar's black hole is 360 million solar masses.

articles.headline: Waymo recalls 4,500 robotaxis for entering closed freeway lanes
articles.summary: Alphabet-owned Waymo is recalling nearly 4,500 self-driving vehicles after incidents of robotaxis entering closed freeway lanes. No collisions or injuries were reported.

articles.headline: Zelensky: Ukraine needs $125bn in external support in 2027
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated Ukraine will need $125 billion in external financial support in 2027, with about $90 billion already committed by the EU for the next year.

articles.headline: Trump may have netted $15m windfall on Nvidia stock
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump may have gained up to $15 million on his Nvidia stock after persuading the company to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang, whose departure followed an affair.

articles.headline: US blacklists Alibaba subsidiary, Megaspeed
articles.summary: The US Commerce Department added Megaspeed and Alibaba's Singapore subsidiary to its trade blacklist over suspected diversion of AI chips to China.

articles.headline: South Korea issues 'take shelter' warning after Russian planes fly near airspace
articles.summary: South Korea scrambled jets and issued a 'take shelter' warning after multiple Russian military planes briefly entered its air defense identification zone.

articles.headline: Trump's Nvidia meme tests limits of presidential decorum
articles.summary: Donald Trump posted a meme of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after his reinstatement, sparking criticism for potentially degrading the presidency and blurring lines between personal interest and public office.

articles.headline: Shanghai party boss Chen Jining probed by anti-graft body
articles.summary: Shanghai's party chief Chen Jining, a Politburo member, is under investigation for 'severe violations of discipline and laws', marking the fourth Politburo member probed since 2025.

articles.headline: JeM commander acknowledges terror network in Rawalakot
articles.summary: Jaish-e-Mohammed commander Masood Ilyas Kashmiri acknowledged his group's network in Rawalakot (POK) and criticized Pakistani authorities over protests and military operations.

articles.headline: 2 Indians among 11 hurt in Houthi attack in Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Two Indians were among 11 people injured when Yemen's Houthi militia targeted a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District.

articles.headline: Pak national first foreigner to visit China space station
articles.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani astronaut, will travel to China's Tiangong space station on Wednesday, becoming the first foreigner to visit the station on a Chinese mission.

articles.headline: Madras HC: Harassment case against TN MLA is sad day for republic
articles.summary: The Madras High Court remarked it is a sad day for the republic that a district collector had to lodge a sexual harassment complaint, stressing confidentiality under the POSH Act.

articles.headline: Bank employee gets dues 48 years after illegal suspension
articles.summary: A bank employee received his dues 48 years after illegal suspension, with the Supreme Court finally closing the case by granting him additional compensation.

articles.headline: DKS, KPCC chief step in to prevent Congress revolt
articles.summary: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar and KPCC chief BK Hariprasad intervened to prevent a revolt by three Congress MLAs over elephant relocation, assuring them of a solution.

articles.headline: 8 injured in leopard attack in UP
articles.summary: A leopard injured eight people working on farms in Kanpur's Maharajpur area after emerging from sugarcane and vegetable fields.

articles.headline: Savarkar’s grandnephew serves legal notice on Sonia Gandhi
articles.summary: Satyaki Savarkar, Vinayak Damodar Savarkar's grandnephew, served a legal notice on Sonia Gandhi over 'questionable' references to the freedom fighter in her memoir.

articles.headline: Bhopal teacher’s e-rickshaw helps bridge school commute gap
articles.summary: A Bhopal teacher bought an e-rickshaw to help students commute to school, addressing transportation and security concerns that led to low attendance.

articles.headline: Govt plans multi-year insurance for cars, bikes
articles.summary: The transport ministry is planning multi-year insurance policies for cars and bikes, aiming to encourage valid insurance coverage and improve compliance.

articles.headline: Modi speaks to Merz ahead of India-EU FTA
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi spoke to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz ahead of the India-EU FTA signing, discussing bilateral trade, investment, and global challenges.

articles.headline: AI is making healthcare smarter, more efficient
articles.summary: AI is revolutionizing healthcare by enabling early detection of critical risks in ECGs, speeding up emergency treatment, and improving diagnostic capabilities.

articles.headline: Diabetes: not just about sugar, but also habits
articles.summary: Dr V Mohan discusses early diabetes screening for Indians, genetic susceptibility, the role of diet and exercise, latest drugs, and the impact of pollution.

articles.headline: Selector must have stature, not just a seat at the table
articles.summary: Former chief selector Dilip Vengsarkar believes selectors travelling with the team must have the stature to challenge the captain and coach for balanced team selection.

articles.headline: Manoj Bajpayee on working with Ram Gopal Varma
articles.summary: Manoj Bajpayee praises Ram Gopal Varma's revolutionary approach and unconventional roles, crediting him for many first-of-their-kind films in his career.

articles.headline: Suniel Shetty's heartwarming tale 'Nanhey Dil' reviewed
articles.summary: The review of 'Nanhey Dil' highlights its wholesome message, innocent charm, and commendable performances, particularly from the young cast.

articles.headline: Nicholas Hoult stars in slick heist thriller 'How to Rob a Bank'
articles.summary: The review of 'How to Rob a Bank' praises its contemporary, socially conscious message, slick narrative, and performances by Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz.

articles.headline: Salman Khan on AI and VFX criticism
articles.summary: Salman Khan sarcastically questioned critics' expertise on AI and VFX regarding his film 'Maatrubhumi', suggesting they focus on soldiers' struggles instead.

articles.headline: AICWA urges security for film stars after threats
articles.summary: AICWA urged Maharashtra CM to increase security for film personalities fearing gangster threats, noting stalled shootings and risks to artistes' livelihoods.

articles.headline: Hollywood props hit auction block, Batpod estimated at £450,000
articles.summary: Iconic movie props, including Batman's Batpod (estimated £450,000-£900,000), Bale's Batsuit, and Harrison Ford's bullwhip, are up for auction.

articles.headline: Thousands flee Don Toliver show after 'unknown substance' sparks panic
articles.summary: Around 12,000 concertgoers were evacuated from a Don Toliver show in Manchester after an unknown substance was released, causing respiratory and eye problems.

articles.headline: Why you should drink coffee & tea lukewarm, not hot
articles.summary: A study suggests drinking beverages above 65°C increases oesophageal cancer risk; lukewarm drinks are recommended to protect the food pipe's inner lining.

articles.headline: Indian investors bullish on AI stocks amid volatility
articles.summary: Indian investors are buying AI stocks like Nvidia, Micron, and Anthropic, building exposure across the AI value chain despite market volatility.

articles.headline: InMobi ramps up hiring, senior hires ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Adtech platform InMobi is increasing hiring, adding 200-250 employees in AI and related fields, and bringing in senior executives ahead of a potential IPO.

articles.headline: Tata Sons could run Rs 17,900cr buyback with board nod
articles.summary: Tata Sons could run a buyback of about Rs 17,900 crore with board approval alone, as it weighs options to provide liquidity to Shapoorji Pallonji Group.

articles.headline: SBI report: 50bps hike can hurt IT cos' growth
articles.summary: SBI economists warned that a 50bps rate hike could hurt IT companies' growth, with ER&D firms like KPIT Technologies facing the sharpest impact.

articles.headline: Public enterprises using AI to improve services
articles.summary: Public sector undertakings like CONCOR and I4C are using AI to enhance logistics efficiency, accelerate responses, and improve cybersecurity.

articles.headline: ETractor finds work off the farm
articles.summary: AutoNxt, an Indian startup, has developed electric, driverless tractors for industrial operators, saving costs on diesel and improving efficiency in applications like biogas plants.

articles.headline: Karnataka lost in transition; Arya's 181, 19 sixes storm
articles.summary: Karnataka's SMAT campaign ended prematurely due to inconsistency and poor returns. Delhi skipper Priyansh Arya's 181, with 19 sixes, set a T20 record.

articles.headline: Stokes in IPL auction; no Mustafizur; 11 from Bangladesh register
articles.summary: Ben Stokes registered for the IPL auction at Rs 2 crore, while 11 Bangladeshi players will participate, but Mustafizur Rahman is not among them.

articles.headline: Grocery prices soar, impacting household budgets
articles.summary: Rising grocery prices, including fruits, vegetables, meat, and staples, are straining household budgets, forcing families to cut back on quality and quantity.

articles.headline: TN MLA C. Arul Vignesh booked for sexual harassment
articles.summary: TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh faces a sexual harassment case after an officer complained about inappropriate messages and alleged misconduct.

articles.headline: Bid ‘responsibly’: RBI to Gsec market makers
articles.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Rohit Jain urged primary dealers (PDs) to bid responsibly in government securities auctions and deepen secondary market liquidity. He flagged concentration in top G-secs, declining demand from institutional investors, and volatile auction prices, emphasizing the need for responsible bidding and market-making.

articles.headline: AI’s rise puts human touch back in demand at workplaces
articles.summary: As AI automates tasks, human qualities like critical thinking, judgement, and ethical decision-making are becoming more valuable. Employers are focusing on humanities and social sciences graduates who can understand human behaviour and societal context.

articles.headline: Risk-based clearances to lift ease of doing biz
articles.summary: Chhattisgarh has attracted ~8 trillion in investments, credited to its ease of doing business policies. The new Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026, categorizes industries by risk, expediting permissions for low-risk sectors.

articles.headline: GSK India to launch seven new cancer treatment molecules
articles.summary: GSK India plans to double its cancer care capacity within 18 months by launching Blenrep and six other oncology molecules. The company aims to reach around 1,000 patients with Blenrep and explores new therapies for lung and other cancers.

articles.headline: Scrapping rules amended; to ease auto firms’ liabilities
articles.summary: The government has amended vehicle scrapping rules, relieving automakers from recording future recycling costs as liabilities. This addresses industry concerns about a potential ~25,000 crore burden under the End-of-Life Vehicles Rules, 2025.

articles.headline: Aluminium body seeks import duty hike, says ₹4 trillion pipeline at risk
articles.summary: The Aluminium Association of India seeks higher import duties to protect a ~4 trillion investment pipeline and promote domestic production. Key demands include increased duty on primary and downstream aluminium and stricter quality norms for scrap.

articles.headline: Blackstone-backed Reit buys Kolkata’s Diamond Plaza for ₹355 cr
articles.summary: Nexus Select Trust, backed by Blackstone, acquired Diamond Plaza Mall in North Kolkata for ~355 crore, expanding its retail portfolio in East India. The mall has a leasable area of 396,609 sq ft.

articles.headline: Sisley Paris expands India lineup, eyes haircare entry
articles.summary: French luxury beauty brand Sisley Paris is expanding in India beyond perfumes, entering skincare and makeup segments. It plans to introduce its haircare brand, Hair Rituel by Sisley, within 18 months.

articles.headline: India, Holland look at boosting cooperation in clean energy
articles.summary: India and the Netherlands (Holland) agreed to strengthen cooperation in shipping, shipbuilding, and green hydrogen, aligning with their strategic partnership and global clean energy initiatives.

articles.headline: Economic activity growth hit 36-month high in October: Icra
articles.summary: India's economic activity grew 12.8% year-on-year in October, the fastest pace in three years, driven by festive season demand and a low base effect, according to Icra.

articles.headline: Labour ministry to push for tax-free EPFO payouts
articles.summary: The Labour Ministry will seek tax-exempt status for EPFO's new systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) and contributions by retired members, aiming for amendments to the Income-Tax Act.

articles.headline: Cashfree’s new wallet lets AI agents pay on users’ behalf
articles.summary: Fintech firm Cashfree launched a wallet allowing AI agents to make payments, with traffic from AI agents growing 16 times. Users link agents to the wallet, setting budgets and rules without sharing card details.

articles.headline: Xiaomi sales fall after memory crunch hits smartphones
articles.summary: Xiaomi reported a 5.2% revenue contraction in Q3, impacted by a global memory crunch and EV division losses. Revenue fell to 107.2 billion yuan, with net income down 68%.

articles.headline: Cosine Robots raises ₹22.36 cr in funding
articles.summary: Bengaluru-based Cosine Robots, developing actuators and motion systems for robotics, raised ₹22.36 crore in a funding round led by Avaana Capital to strengthen R&D and production.

articles.headline: Muni bond issues may pick up in Q4
articles.summary: Municipal bond issuances could rise in Q4FY27 with 15-20 issues in the pipeline. Higher yields, wider credit spreads, and long approval processes may delay many, with a meaningful pick-up possible in H1FY28.

articles.headline: 26% of vehicles registered in Delhi since FY18 aren’t BS-VI
articles.summary: Around 26% of vehicles registered in Delhi since FY18 do not meet BS-VI emission norms. This contributes to air pollution, with transport being a major source of PM2.5 in the Delhi-NCR region.

articles.headline: Axis Bank leads credit card additions in October
articles.summary: Axis Bank added the most credit cards in October, while HDFC Bank saw net additions fall sharply. Overall credit card additions grew 19.7% month-on-month, with spending up 14% year-on-year.

articles.headline: ~ gains despite stronger $; sharp fall may amplify shocks: Report
articles.summary: A SBI report notes the rupee's appreciation against a strengthening dollar, arguing excessive depreciation could amplify economic shocks. It suggests a 25 bps rate hike for financial stability.

articles.headline: India to field 70-member team for BIMSTEC U-23
articles.summary: Over 200 athletes from six countries will compete in the BIMSTEC Under-23 Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar. India will field a 70-member contingent.

articles.headline: Bima Sugam launch deferred amid insurer readiness gaps
articles.summary: The Bima Sugam insurance marketplace launch is deferred to end-December due to gaps in insurer readiness and compliance with a new four-tier motor insurance framework.

articles.headline: ‘Plan to make Bastar heaven on Earth’
articles.summary: Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai plans to develop Bastar as a leading tribal division and global tourism hub, focusing on connectivity, irrigation, education, and employment through various schemes.

articles.headline: Zojila tunnel likely to be built in next 6-8 months: Gadkari
articles.summary: Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari stated the Zojila tunnel, Asia's longest, will be completed in 6-8 months. 70% of the excavation work is done, promising all-weather connectivity to Ladakh.

articles.headline: A regulatory cadre for India
articles.summary: The author suggests creating a dedicated regulatory cadre through UPSC recruitment and structured training to enhance expertise and independence in India's regulatory bodies.

articles.headline: 7 Budget recommendations for infra
articles.summary: Recommendations for the infrastructure sector include increased rail budget, UMTA implementation, group taxation for infra SPVs, ring-fencing monetization proceeds, and a larger project pipeline.

articles.headline: A Historian In Gaza by Jean-Pierre Filiu
articles.summary: Jean-Pierre Filiu's book 'A Historian In Gaza' offers a firsthand account of the destruction and human suffering in Gaza, detailing systematic attacks and the challenges of survival.

articles.headline: Back at Nvidia’s helm, Huang vows to be ‘a better CEO’
articles.summary: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO, vowing to be better. The board's decision was influenced by Trump, with the company facing scrutiny over its handling of AI chip exports and geopolitical risks.

articles.headline: India Inc’s earnings charge puts bulls back in saddle
articles.summary: Strong Q2FY27 results, with a 30.4% net profit rise, have boosted market sentiment. Oil and gas, metals, power, and automotives led growth, while IT and pharma lagged.

articles.headline: Protein inflation rises on feed, fodder costs
articles.summary: Retail inflation for protein products like milk, eggs, and meat has risen due to low monsoon rainfall, rising feed and fodder costs, and maize diversion for ethanol.

articles.headline: India Inc must create quality jobs, accelerate investment: CII prez
articles.summary: CII President R Mukundan urged Indian industry to accelerate investment, create quality jobs, and improve productivity, emphasizing the need to match government reforms with greater commitment.

articles.headline: Ease of doing business remains state-level challenge: USISPF chief
articles.summary: USISPF President Mukesh Aghi highlighted ease of doing business at the state level as a challenge, urging states to match central government reforms for attracting foreign investment.

articles.headline: Private credit funds seek distinct status under AIF framework
articles.summary: Private credit funds are seeking a separate category under the AIF framework from Sebi, citing differences in business models, leverage restrictions, and taxation challenges.

articles.headline: IIFCL IPO: Govt to offload partial stake
articles.summary: The government plans a partial stake sale in IIFCL through an IPO, with work underway to file a draft paper with Sebi by end of the financial year.

articles.headline: US markets slide, Asian markets rebound as Nvidia rally fizzles out
articles.summary: US markets fell, led by tech stocks, amid concerns over tariffs and AI safety. Asian markets rebounded, with South Korea and Japan showing gains.

articles.headline: Tile makers outperform peers; Cera remains preferred pick
articles.summary: The tile sector outperformed peers in Q2FY27 with strong revenue growth and improved margins. Cera Sanitaryware is a preferred pick due to benefits from price hikes and attractive valuations.

articles.headline: RBI has already answered its own listing question
articles.summary: The author argues that RBI's existing regulations for NBFCs ensure transparency and governance without mandating listing, questioning the necessity for Tata Sons to list.

articles.headline: Himalayan reset: Nepal PM’s state visit signals a thaw
articles.summary: Nepal PM Balendra Shah's state visit to India aims to reset bilateral relations, focusing on civilisational links and economic cooperation, including a $1.6 billion aid package.

articles.headline: India, Canada 'very close' to concluding trade pact talks
articles.summary: Negotiators from India and Canada are in active discussions to finalize a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). Sources indicate the two sides are 'very close' to concluding the negotiations, which were initially launched to boost bilateral trade and investment. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau had previously set a target to conclude talks by March.

articles.headline: Scindia announces advisory panel to resolve telecom startup, MSME issues
articles.summary: Telecom Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has announced a new advisory committee to resolve issues faced by startups and MSMEs in the telecom sector. The panel will address regulatory hurdles and help local companies achieve self-reliance in technology, acting as a facilitator for product development and commercialisation.

articles.headline: Investors question fairness of Tata Steel APL Apollo deal over debt concerns
articles.summary: Minority shareholders and proxy advisory firms have criticized the ₹28,000-crore deal between APL Apollo Tubes and Tata Steel as unfair. Concerns center on the complex transaction structure and potential for increased debt for Tata Steel, adding ~₹4,200 crore in new liabilities. The deal implies a significant premium, raising questions about benefits for retail investors.

articles.headline: RBI Deputy Governor flags narrowing buyer base for government securities
articles.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Rohit Jain urged primary dealers to actively promote government securities (G-Secs) to retail investors due to weakening institutional demand and liquidity concentration. Dealers are encouraged to expand market-making in less-traded securities and improve pricing accuracy to deepen the bond market.

articles.headline: Bisleri assures safety after FSSAI flags single batch for high bromate levels
articles.summary: Bisleri International clarified that its bottled water is safe across all 143 plants after FSSAI flagged a single batch from its Goa facility for high bromate levels. The company stated subsequent samples met all safety standards and prosecution was sanctioned based on an initial report.

articles.headline: SBI Mutual Fund gets RBI nod to acquire up to 9.99% in South Indian Bank
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has approved SBI Mutual Fund's proposal to acquire up to 9.99% stake in South Indian Bank, subject to compliance with banking regulations and holding the stake for investment purposes only.

articles.headline: Shadowfax acquires WeFast for ₹23.3 crore to expand intra-city delivery
articles.summary: Logistics startup Shadowfax has acquired WeFast India for ₹23.3 crore to expand its presence in the on-demand intra-city delivery market. The deal includes WeFast's technology, customer base, and courier network, integrating hyperlocal fulfillment with Shadowfax's services.

articles.headline: Modi, German Chancellor Merz review strategic partnership, discuss global issues
